reused_precedent.note: No new procedure invented. Re-ran the exact mechanism documented by three prior completed UMRs, read directly from their umr_tasks rows and /opt/veridian/ai-os/reports/*.json evidence files.
reused_precedent.mechanism: Delete ONLY the workspace/ subdirectory of a task dir whose task.yaml status is terminal, gated by (a) systemctl --user is-active <service> not active/activating/reloading, (b) git status --porcelain clean in the workspace, (c) an upstream exists and has zero unpushed commits. Never touch task.yaml, review.json, supervisor.log, supervisor-result.json, pr_url.txt, prompt.txt, or the task dir root itself.
reused_sanctioned_tools: cron_systemd_state_manager capability (systemctl --user is-active/stop/start) for both the workspace-reclaim unit-safety gate and for making the live DB quiescent before VACUUM

step3a_vacuum.decision: PROCEED -- own live PRAGMA integrity_check run immediately before acting returned 'ok' (page_count 992941, freelist_count 390455 @ 4096B pages, matching the spec's ~396000-page / ~1.5GB estimate almost exactly). This directly contradicts what UMR-20260807-001537-787a and UMR-20260807-001650-d266 found ~8h earlier (both independently reproduced a genuine 'database disk image is malformed' / wiring_registry index corruption) -- the DB has evidently been repaired since then. Re-verified myself, live, right before acting -- did not trust the spec's claim or the stale prior findings blindly.
step3a_vacuum.quiescence: Stopped both DB-writing timers (veridian-cron-dispatch-tick.timer, veridian-pm-report-tick.timer) via systemctl --user stop; confirmed both services AND timers inactive; confirmed no open fds via fuser/lsof before proceeding; restarted both timers immediately after VACUUM completed and verified integrity.

Backup's own PRAGMA integrity_check verified 'ok' before VACUUM proceeded. step3b_dispatch_tick_cron_log.decision: PROCEED -- truncated in place (`: > file`, inode preserved)
step3b_dispatch_tick_cron_log.reasoning: Read the file directly: tail is a full JSON state dump (real_task_counts, blocked-task list, etc.) re-appended in full every ~5min cron tick, confirming the spec's claim first-hand. Checked the owning systemd unit (veridian-cron-dispatch-tick.service): Type=oneshot with StandardOutput/StandardError=append:<this file>, invoked fresh every ~5min by its own timer -- no long-lived process holds this file open, so truncating in place is safe and the next tick will simply reopen-and-append to the now-empty file. Grepped all scripts for read/parse references to this specific log path: none found beyond the unit's own write redirect, so nothing depends on its accumulated history.
